item.title: China’s Leader Xi Seeks to Extend Truce with Trump During U.S. Summit
item.description: Facing an American president constrained by war and politics, China’s leader may seek to lock in a tactical truce while he shores up a fragile economy at home.
item.dc:creator: David Pierson
item.media:description: President Trump and the Chinese leader, Xi Jinping, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing in May.

item.title: China’s Continued Control of Rare Earths Looms Over Trump-Xi Meeting
item.description: Manufacturers are struggling with constrained supplies as U.S. and Chinese officials negotiate over export restrictions with consequences for global industry.
item.dc:creator: Keith Bradsher
item.media:description: A display about rare-earth production at the National Museum in Beijing.

item.title: Japan Meets With Trump, Hoping to Get His Help on China
item.description: Japan’s prime minister will meet President Trump to discuss China’s economic and security pressure while also seeking to de-escalate tensions with Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Javier C. Hernández and Lily Kuo
item.media:description: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi of Japan in a meeting with President Trump, who is not pictured, in Tokyo last year. Ms. Takaichi remains focused on persuading Mr. Trump to maintain security commitments in East Asia.

item.title: Wall Street Is Growing Skeptical of the Data Center Boom
item.description: Several companies tied to the data center industry have delayed their initial public offerings amid the increasing public backlash to these energy guzzling facilities.
item.dc:creator: Maureen Farrell
item.media:description: Meta’s new data center in Middleton Township, Ohio. Some companies are delaying plans to raise tens of billions of dollars in public markets to fund the build-out of A.I. infrastructure.

item.title: Are A.I. Models Being Misled to Act Too Human?
item.description: A corporate spat between two tech giants last week was just the latest volley in a conflict over whether dangerous mistakes are being made in A.I. training.
item.dc:creator: Cade Metz
item.media:credit: Chona Kasinger for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mustafa Suleyman, Microsoft’s A.I. chief, argued in an essay published Wednesday that the tech start-up Anthropic was pushing its systems too hard to mimic human behaviors.

item.title: Spectre of Rogue A.I. Looms Over U.N. Talks on Digital Cooperation
item.description: Diplomats, dignitaries and tech experts gathered amid the United Nations General Assembly to debate how to address the threats and harness the potential of artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Ephrat Livni
item.media:credit: Angelina Katsanis for The New York Times
item.media:description: The United Nations headquarters on Monday as world leaders convened in New York for the General Assembly.

item.title: Trump Faces the Sting of a Media Boycott After Press Pool Withdrawal
item.description: A boycott of the White House press pool by the major networks deprives the president of the oxygen of screen time. But he is still finding ways to get on the air.
item.dc:creator: Peter Baker
item.media:credit: Pete Marovich for The New York Times
item.media:description: Television is how President Trump’s allies and even his aides communicate with him.

item.title: Trump and Mamdani Show Their Unlikely Rapport, This Time in New York
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani invited the president to his official residence in Manhattan, where the two spoke about policing, immigration and affordable housing.
item.dc:creator: Jeffery C. Mays, Ed Shanahan and Luis Ferré-Sadurní
item.media:credit: Dave Sanders for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani hosted President Trump on Monday at Gracie Mansion.

item.title: Trump’s U.N. Speech Comes at a Time of Tumult
item.description: The president, who has been dogged by the war in Iran and eroding alliances, is also expected to sign a security deal on Greenland and meet with world leaders.
item.dc:creator: Zolan Kanno-Youngs and David E. Sanger
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Angelina Katsanis for The New York Times
item.media:description: The 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly will start this week in New York City.

item.title: Earl Spencer Book Blasts Diana’s Treatment by UK Royal Family
item.description: The decades have not lessened Earl Spencer’s anger over the House of Windsor’s treatment of the former Princess of Wales. King Charles comes in for special vitriol.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Lyall
item.media:description: Earl Spencer, during an interview with the BBC this month. His new book, “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister,” comes out on Tuesday.

item.title: Book Review: “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister,” by Charles Spencer
item.description: “Swan Song,” Charles Spencer’s memoir of Lady Diana, is full of love and vengeance.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Jacobs

item.media:description: Princess Diana

item.title: Takeaways From Charles Spencer’s Memoir, “Swan Song,” About Princess Diana
item.description: Nearly 30 years after Princess Diana died, her brother has written a book about her life, her marriage to Prince Charles and the suffering she endured at the hands of the tabloid press.
item.dc:creator: The Book Review

item.title: South Korean President Calls for Easing Sanctions on the North
item.description: President Trump should demand that North Korea freeze, not eliminate, its nuclear weapons program, President Lee Jae Myung said in an interview.
item.dc:creator: Choe Sang-Hun
item.category: Arms Control and Limitation and Disarmament
item.media:credit: Chang W. Lee/The New York Times
item.media:description: President Lee Jae Myung spoke with The New York Times for about 70 minutes at the Blue House, the presidential compound in Seoul.

item.title: Princeton Is No Longer No. 1 in the U.S. News Rankings
item.description: The Massachusetts Institute for Technology pulled ahead on a set of criteria that are as contentious as they are influential.
item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder
item.media:credit: Sophie Park for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Massachusetts Institute of Technology, in Cambridge, Mass., is now No. 1, according to U.S. News & World Report.

item.title: German Leaders Prepare to Deny Far Right Access to Secret War Plan
item.description: With the Alternative for Germany party close to power in a German state, federal officials are planning to limit the group’s access to classified intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Jim Tankersley, Christopher F. Schuetze and Philip Kaleta
item.media:description: The State Parliament in Saxony-Anhalt, a state in eastern Germany where the AfD could soon take power.

item.title: Man Shot by ICE Agent Says His Car Was Struck Twice Before He Was Shot
item.description: A Venezuelan immigrant, Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, was shot in Austin, Texas, on Sunday after a traffic stop. The shooting prompted calls from local officials for a transparent investigation.
item.dc:creator: Christina Morales, Hamed Aleaziz and Billy Witz
item.media:description: Police tape surrounds the location where local authorities say a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer shot and wounded a man in Austin, Texas, on Sunday.

item.title: George W. Bush and Cornyn Leave Out Paxton as They Raise Cash for Senate Candidates
item.description: The former president and Texas senator are headlining a fund-raiser in Dallas for top Republican Senate candidates. Not included: Ken Paxton, the nominee in their own state.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner and Theodore Schleifer
item.media:credit: Kenny Holston/The New York Times; Hiroko Masuike/The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator John Cornyn of Texas, left, lost a costly and bitter Republican primary this year to Ken Paxton, the state attorney general, right. Former President George W. Bush, center, has mostly stayed out of the fray, but his politics align more with Mr. Cornyn’s.

item.title: Appeals Court Sides With Missouri Republicans on Redrawn House Map
item.description: The order may have little impact because of a U.S. Supreme Court ruling that blocked the congressional districts that favor Republicans.
item.dc:creator: Mitch Smith
item.media:description: Secretary of State Denny Hoskins of Missouri, a Republican, said he believed redistricting was not eligible for a referendum.

item.title: House Democrat Crosses Party Lines to Endorse Rep. Mike Lawler in Midterms Race
item.description: Representative Mike Lawler, a Republican seeking re-election in a swing district in New York, was backed by Representative Jared Golden, Democrat of Maine.
item.dc:creator: Grace Ashford
item.media:description: Representative Mike Lawler, a Republican, is trying to fend off a challenge from Cait Conley, a Democrat, in a critical House swing district in New York.

item.title: JB Pritzker Says He Used GLP-1s to Lose 80 Pounds
item.description: Gov. JB Pritzker of Illinois, widely seen as a potential presidential candidate, revealed in an interview on “CBS Mornings” that he had been on a GLP-1 regimen since 2024.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein
item.media:description: Gov. JB Pritzker of Illinois is not the first potential presidential hopeful to make getting in better shape part of their campaign preparations.

item.title: David George Gordon, Apostle for Bugs on the Dinner Plate, Dies at 76
item.description: His “The Eat-a-Bug Cookbook” made a case for insects as food, while his boisterous cooking demonstrations brought tarantulas and crickets to TV.
item.dc:creator: Michael S. Rosenwald

item.title: Italy’s Prisons Were Overcrowded. Then They Overheated.
item.description: As temperatures in the country continue to approach 90 degrees Fahrenheit, inmates have been sleeping on concrete cell floors. Even the guards have complained.
item.dc:creator: Elisabetta Povoledo
item.media:description: Outside the Rebibbia prison in Rome. There are nearly 65,000 inmates in Italian detention facilities, crammed into cells built for less than 47,000.
